inspection_summary: Inspected all 589 normalized lines. The source develops a complete local-to-global certification pipeline: encode RH by the real-zero threshold of a heat-deformed entire-function family; turn an exceptionally close consecutive zero pair into a lower bound for the de Bruijn-Newman constant; and control the pair's global interaction by combining a finite computed zero window with analytic zero-counting tails. Sixteen materially distinct units are retained. Formula-layout damage is explicitly isolated at lines 397-401 and 493-523, while several broader units whose prose remains recoverable are marked as requiring scan verification before formula-level reuse.

sections_inspected.label: Publication matter, abstract, and scope
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the improved lower bound and identifies a close consecutive zero pair as the enabling evidence; publication metadata and indexing terms supply no independent mechanism.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the heat-deformed cosine-transform family, relates its zero geometry to RH and the de Bruijn-Newman threshold, represents the family through its zeros, and states the Lehmer-pair lower-bound criterion.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Application of Theorem 1.1
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds a zero-density tail estimate, identifies and computes around the close pair, decomposes and bounds the global interaction sum, certifies the Lehmer condition, and derives and interprets the new lower bound.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Appendix and acknowledgement
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Supplies the quantitative proof of the unit-interval zero-count bound used in the tail estimate; the final acknowledgement is nonmathematical.

sections_inspected.label: References
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic support only; no new source-local mathematical mechanism.

accepted_units.title: Heat-deformed cosine transform turns RH into a real-zero condition
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces the deformation family H_t and records that H_0 is a rescaled xi-function, so RH can be viewed as a statement about the zero geometry of one member of a continuous transform family. This is the representation on which every later threshold and close-pair argument operates.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the definition-to-equivalence chain; the later flow threshold in u002 supplies the dynamical interpretation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed formulas (1.1)-(1.3) have extraction-layout damage. Only the prose-supported transform relation, the H_0/xi scaling, and the real-zero equivalence are accepted; verify the original scan before reusing exact kernels or normalizations.

accepted_units.title: Monotone real-zero flow and the de Bruijn-Newman threshold
accepted_units.why_material: Combines persistence of real zeros under increasing deformation time with a sharp threshold Λ, identifies RH with Λ at most zero, and explains Newman's opposite inequality as the claim that RH is at the boundary of instability under perturbation.
accepted_units.context_note: Read with the H_t definition and H_0 equivalence in u001; line 55 attributes the two opening properties to de Bruijn but intervening lines are publication footnotes and page furniture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose and threshold statement are legible in the normalized text; no formula reconstruction is needed.

accepted_units.title: Hadamard product encodes H_t by a summable symmetric zero set
accepted_units.why_material: Re-expresses the entire function as a product over squared zero locations, records inverse-square summability, and fixes an even indexing convention. This converts an analytic-function question into controllable geometry and sums over zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: Provides the convergence and indexing infrastructure required by the Lehmer interaction quantity in u004 and its later decomposition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The product layout is somewhat displaced but the prose, product factors, summability statement, and symmetry convention remain readable; scan verification is advisable for exact factor typography.

accepted_units.title: Lehmer pairs compare a tiny gap with interaction from all other zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Defines a Lehmer pair by multiplying the squared gap between consecutive simple positive zeros by an interaction sum over every other signed zero. The criterion compresses a global zero configuration into one local-gap-versus-background test.
accepted_units.context_note: The inverse-square convergence in u003 explains why the interaction sum is well-defined; the running header at lines 141-149 is inert page furniture inside the continued definition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The summation formula is readable apart from ordinary PDF layout artifacts; its excluded indices and signed-zero range are clarified in prose.

accepted_units.title: A Lehmer pair yields a quantitative lower bound for Λ
accepted_units.why_material: States the bridge from static zero geometry to heat-flow obstruction: nonpositive interaction would force Λ positive, while positive interaction produces an explicit negative λ_k bounded above by Λ.
accepted_units.context_note: Depends on the gap and interaction definitions in u004 and is instantiated only after u013 certifies the selected pair.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The case split and bound are prose-clear; verify the exact exponent and normalization in formula (1.13) against the scan before symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: Backlund zero counting gives a unit-interval density bound
accepted_units.why_material: Turns a global zero-counting formula with explicit error control into the local estimate N(T+1)-N(T) at most log T above a fixed height. This supplies a coarse but certified density envelope for uncomputed zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The appendix proof is retained separately as u016; u007 consumes this local density bound to control an inverse-square tail.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The principal zero-count formula has minor layout damage, but its role and the explicit error and unit-interval bounds are legible; exact constants should be scan-checked before recomputation.

accepted_units.title: Convert local zero counts into an inverse-square tail bound
accepted_units.why_material: Groups zeros into unit-height bins, bounds each bin using u006, and compares the resulting logarithm-weighted reciprocal-square series with an integral. This is a reusable route from density control to a summable global tail estimate.
accepted_units.context_note: Assumes Λ<0 so the H_0 zeros are real and correspond to zeta ordinates; the bound is later applied at the far-window endpoint in u012.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Summation alignment in lines 225-237 is degraded, but the binning, appeal to Lemma 2.1, integral comparison, and resulting bound are recoverable from checked prose. Verify the scan before formula-level extraction.

accepted_units.title: Targeted high-precision computation around an exceptional close pair
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why a known close consecutive pair was recomputed with many neighbors at high precision, why only a relatively small local window may suffice for the global interaction estimate, and why the search evidence does not establish that the pair is globally optimal.
accepted_units.context_note: Supplies the empirical target and search limitations for the analytic decomposition beginning in u009; it distinguishes verified local computation from heuristic confidence that no better early pair was missed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The decimal zero data and index are legible, but any numerical replay should use the retained original rather than retyped extracted typography.

accepted_units.title: Partition the global interaction into local, intermediate, and remote blocks
accepted_units.why_material: Decomposes g_K into a finite block centered on the close pair, a large asymmetric intermediate block, and a remote two-sided tail. The partition lets each region be controlled by the information best suited to it rather than demanding all zeros at equal precision.
accepted_units.context_note: Sets n=9998 and defines the three quantities bounded independently in u010-u012; the running header at lines 280-288 does not alter the definitions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The three displayed sums are sufficiently readable together with the prose, though their exact index endpoints should be checked against the scan before implementation.

accepted_units.title: Bound the finite local block by the two adjacent outer gaps
accepted_units.why_material: Uses realness and simplicity under the Λ<0 branch to dominate every term in the local computed block by distances to the nearest zero outside the close pair, reducing thousands of terms to two measured neighboring gaps and an explicit conservative bound.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the local contribution M_K,n in u009; its numerical inputs are the four consecutive ordinates displayed in (2.8).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The inequality chain and ordinates are readable. Exact upward rounding and decimal values remain representation-sensitive and should be checked against the original for numerical reuse.

accepted_units.title: Bound the intermediate block by its nearest endpoint distance
accepted_units.why_material: Controls the many remaining inner-side terms by a common worst-case separation and the number of terms, replacing a large uncomputed block by one computed endpoint ordinate and yielding a small explicit contribution.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the I_K,n+1 contribution from u009 and complements the local-gap bound u010 and remote-tail bound u012.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The extracted display is vertically fragmented but the endpoint-distance bound, substituted ordinate, and final value are readable; confirm exact factors from the scan before calculation.

accepted_units.title: Use evenness, monotone distance ratios, and zero density to bound the remote tail
accepted_units.why_material: Folds the negative and positive remote zeros together using evenness, factors remote denominators into endpoint-dependent ratios times inverse-square zero weights, and invokes u007 to control the infinite remainder. This closes a finite-computation certificate for a genuinely global interaction sum.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the R_K,K+n+2 term from u009 and uses the computed far endpoint together with the analytic inverse-square tail bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Lines 397-401 are formula-damaged and quarantined in coverage: the exact monotonic-ratio expression is not reconstructed. The surrounding prose and formulas (2.12)-(2.15) support the qualitative bounding mechanism and final bound, but scan verification is required before exact derivation or training use.

accepted_units.title: Aggregate the three bounds to certify the close pair as Lehmer
accepted_units.why_material: Adds the independently controlled interaction blocks, combines the resulting global upper bound with the accurately measured tiny gap, and verifies the Lehmer inequality by a wide margin.
accepted_units.context_note: Consumes the decomposition u009 and component bounds u010-u012; it is the certificate needed before applying the abstract theorem u005.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The aggregate bounds, gap value, and Lehmer comparison are legible; numerical transcription should still be verified from the original scan.

accepted_units.title: Monotonicity converts a conservative interaction bound into the new Λ bound
accepted_units.why_material: Handles the Λ≥0 branch trivially, then under Λ<0 uses monotonic decrease of λ_k with the interaction value to feed the certified upper bound into the Lehmer theorem and obtain the stated lower bound for Λ.
accepted_units.context_note: Makes the proof's assumption fork explicit and depends on u005 and u013; it is a lower-bound result, not a proof of either RH or Newman's conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The logical case split, monotonicity statement, and final numerical bound are prose-clear and do not require restoring a damaged formula.

accepted_units.title: The close-pair gap dominates sensitivity to the interaction estimate
accepted_units.why_material: Explains through a small-parameter expansion that the leading gap-squared term already nearly equals the reported Λ bound, so substantial conservatism in the global interaction estimate has little effect. This clarifies why the certification can succeed without highly accurate knowledge of every zero.
accepted_units.context_note: Interprets the numerical stability of the u014 conclusion after u013 shows the gap-interaction product is very small.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Taylor-series typography in lines 476-485 is damaged. Only the prose-supported insensitivity claim and the separately legible leading-term magnitude are retained; verify the full expansion and signs in the original scan before reuse.

accepted_units.title: Explicit error absorption proves the unit-interval zero-count certificate
accepted_units.why_material: Separates the smooth main term from the zero-counting error, bounds the main-term increment using a logarithmic expansion, and absorbs logarithmic-error and constant terms into fractions of log T above the stated threshold, establishing the local density estimate used in u007.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the source's internal certificate for u006 and therefore closes the analytic dependency behind the remote-tail calculation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Lines 493-523 contain severe formula-layout damage and are quarantined rather than reconstructed. Prose at lines 524-525 identifies the alternating-series bound, and lines 525-566 preserve the subsequent explicit inequalities, but the entire derivation requires original-scan verification before formula-level use.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Close-pair geometry as a heat-flow obstruction
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The heat-deformation representation turns RH into a threshold question, while the Lehmer criterion converts an unusually small local zero gap, after global-background certification, into a quantitative obstruction to pushing the all-real-zero regime too far below time zero.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The conclusion is a solver- and pair-specific lower bound for Λ under an explicit case split; it neither proves RH nor establishes Λ≥0.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Finite-window certificate for a global zero interaction
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A global sum over all zeros can be certified from finitely many accurate local zeros by partitioning it into regions, using nearest-endpoint domination on finite blocks, and applying a zero-density-derived inverse-square bound to the infinite tail.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This certificate uses the Λ<0 real-zero branch and contains formula-sensitive tail steps that require the original scan before exact replay.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Why a conservative global estimate still yields a sharp lower bound
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Once the gap-interaction product is tiny, the leading gap-squared contribution controls the Lehmer lower bound, making the final Λ estimate insensitive to coarse upper control of the background interaction.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The full Taylor expansion is extraction-damaged, and the stability conclusion is local to the small-product regime documented for this pair.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Zero counting as the analytic backstop for computation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: An explicit global counting formula can be converted into unit-interval density control and then into a convergent inverse-square tail estimate, providing analytic coverage beyond the computed zero window.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The constants and threshold are those stated in this source, and the appendix's formula-damaged main-term algebra needs scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Strong numerical evidence without an optimality claim
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Targeted high-precision computation around a spectacularly close pair supports a rigorously derived improved Λ bound even though the broader search procedure does not conclusively rule out a better pair among the zeros considered.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source reports limited search completeness and therefore supports the achieved bound, not global optimality of the selected pair.

within_source_saturation: Saturated for source-grounded semantic planning: every mathematical section, including the appendix proof, is represented by distinct units or explicitly marked as supporting, routine, front matter, or extraction-defective. Further subdivision would chiefly separate routine numerical substitution from the represented local/intermediate/tail mechanisms or would require reconstructing quarantined formulas.
stop_reason: All 589 normalized lines were inspected and exactly partitioned. The retained units cover the deformation threshold, zero-product representation, Lehmer bridge, zero-density machinery, computational targeting, three-region interaction certificate, final lower bound, stability explanation, and appendix certification; the only unrecoverable formula spans are explicitly quarantined, and remaining lines are page furniture, summary, acknowledgement, or references.
